idiom_name: typed fragment functions / TSX components; hbs/EJS partials for file-based templates
implementation_notes: TypeScript's version of the pattern is one fragment per function or component behind a props interface: fragments are composed by nesting (page -> layout -> row) and the compiler checks that every call site supplies the required data - a function returning a string, or a TSX component rendered by React/Preact server rendering (renderToString/renderToStaticMarkup) or a JSX-capable server framework. Where templates stay in files, the engine keeps working under types: Express/NestJS use hbs (Handlebars) with .hbs partials, registered via registerPartial and rendered with typed models, and EJS includes take the same typed locals object. Prefer typed functions/components in new code; keep engine partials where designers own the markup.
pitfalls: A fragment typed as returning string says nothing about being the right markup: escaping must be centralized (one escape helper or the engine's escaped output), because the compiler cannot catch an unescaped interpolation.
TSX fragments must be rendered, not stringified - String(<Row />) yields "[object Object]", so use the renderer's server entry point; also keep one render pass per page to avoid diverging HTML.
Partial-based stacks (hbs/EJS) are untyped by default: declare the render model at the call site and keep partial names in one typed registry, or a renamed partial only fails at request time.
